_comment: Pinned static ffmpeg/ffprobe builds for the desktop sidecar (ADR-0019 §3).
Checksums are per-platform because a release ships both Apple Silicon and
Intel artifacts, and the two architectures are different binaries. Each tool
pins two digests: `archive_sha256` is checked before the download is
unpacked, `sha256` is checked on the extracted binary and re-checked by
build_sidecar.py before it is allowed into a bundle.
Omit `archive_member` when a URL serves the binary directly rather than a
zip containing it.
What was verified for the pinned macOS builds (2026-07-22), rather than
taken from the label:
- genuinely static: `otool -L` lists only /usr/lib and /System/Library
entries, so there is no third-party dylib closure to leave behind. A
package-manager ffmpeg fails exactly here — Homebrew's is a thin binary
over its own prefix, so a copy runs on the build machine and nowhere
else.
- redistributable: `--enable-gpl --enable-version3` with NO
`--enable-nonfree`. This is the check that disqualified the popular
eugeneware/ffmpeg-static builds, which are static and well-maintained but
carry `--enable-nonfree` and therefore may not be distributed at all.
- `--enable-libx264`, which media/hls.py needs for the transcode ladder;
only the remux path is `-c:v copy`, so an LGPL build would silently lose
transcoding.
- signed and notarized (Developer ID: Martin Riedl, KU3N25YGLU), which is
stronger than the ad-hoc signature ADR-0019 §4 treats as the floor.
Staging copies bytes and sets the execute bit, neither of which
invalidates a Mach-O signature — but anything that later rewrites these
binaries must re-sign them.
linux-x86_64 is deliberately unpinned. The same builder's Linux artifacts add
`--enable-decklink`, which forces `--enable-nonfree` and makes them
non-redistributable; and Linux is not a release target (plan 3 D7 ships
Apple Silicon + Intel). The container deployment is unaffected — it uses the
image's own ffmpeg (ADR-0005). Build with --skip-ffmpeg on Linux; the
sidecar then falls back to a system ffmpeg via media/tool_paths.py.
To refresh a pin: pick the build, verify the four properties above, record
the URLs and both digests here, then run `python packaging/fetch_ffmpeg.py`.
